metadata.notes: agent_supports: partial (vibe raises the scenario's trigger-2 dialog — the first-use workspace trust prompt — but only at launch, from run_cli BEFORE load_session, so no send can elicit it and no live session exists for the arc; sandbox and MCP-elicitation triggers are absent, and the only two mid-session blocking waits both belong to a tool call); daemon_capability: incapable (no session directory exists at dialog time, nothing is written, and the one installed hook fires at turn end); driver_capability: ready

assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: partial (Mistral Vibe 2.19.1 DOES raise a tool-less blocking dialog — the first-use workspace trust prompt, which is trigger #2 in the scenario's own list — plus a startup update prompt and two teardown y/N prompts. But EVERY one of them is a launch-time or exit-time gate raised outside the AgentLoop, so none can be elicited by a `send` and none can produce the `working → waiting` arc the row asserts. The other three triggers are absent outright.)
daemon_capability: incapable (at dialog time there is no session for the arc to attach to — the transcript directory is created lazily on the first save — and even when one exists from a prior run, nothing is written and the one installed hook fires at turn end)
driver_capability: ready (send/keys/wait_turn/sleep/restart are all in DRIVE_ELICITS; the missing piece is not a driver primitive)

## Scenario signal

2.27 asserts `ready → working → waiting` entered while a dialog with NO tool call in flight is on screen, `waiting → working → ready` after the user answers with nothing completing to carry the release, and a final `ready` surviving a >=15s trailing idle — the load-bearing phase, which catches a session left pinned at `waiting`.

## Which triggers vibe has, and where they fire (agent_supports: partial)

I checked all four of the scenario's triggers against the installed 2.19.1 package:

1. **Sandbox / network-access confirmation — ABSENT.** A case-insensitive scan of the whole `vibe/` package for `sandbox` returns zero hits. Vibe has no sandbox to confirm out of.
2. **First-use trust prompt for the workspace — PRESENT, but pre-session.** `TrustFolderDialog` (setup/trusted_folders/trust_folder_dialog.py) is a real modal with TRUST_REPO / TRUST_CWD / TRUST_SESSION / DECLINE options, built by `maybe_build_workspace_trust_prompt` (core/trusted_folders.py:118). It is raised from `check_and_resolve_trusted_folder` (cli/entrypoint.py:173), invoked as the `resolve_trusted_folder` callback in `run_cli` at cli/cli.py:458-460 — which is BEFORE `load_session` (:481) and before `_run_interactive_mode` (:485). At that moment no `AgentLoop`, no `SessionLogger` and no `~/.vibe/logs/session/<id>/` exist. There is no session, no turn, and no way for a `send` to reach it.
3. **Server-driven MCP elicitation — ABSENT.** A case-insensitive scan for `elicit` across the package returns zero hits. Vibe's MCP surface (core/tools/mcp/{pool,registry,tools}.py, mcp_settings.py, mcp_sampling.py) has no elicitation handler. The MCP OAuth and connector-auth modals (cli/textual_ui/widgets/{mcp_oauth_app,connector_auth_app}.py) exist but are raised from `MCPApp` messages — i.e. the user's own `/mcp` slash command, from the idle input app, with no turn in flight.
4. **Auto-mode / settings review — ABSENT in the blocking sense.** `_maybe_run_startup_update_prompt` (cli/cli.py:360-380, :457) is a blocking startup dialog, but it runs even earlier than (2), at :457. `cli/plan_offer/` is not a dialog at all: `plan_offer_cta` returns CTA text appended to a message body (app.py:3979-3983). The model / theme / thinking / config / proxy pickers are user-invoked slash commands. Two `input()` y/N prompts exist (entrypoint.py:223, :241 — worktree removal and branch deletion) and run AFTER `run_cli` returns, at teardown.

**Mid-session, vibe has exactly two blocking waits, and both belong to a tool call.** The TUI holds precisely two futures: `_pending_approval`, awaited by `_approval_callback` (app.py:2008-2034) for a tool permission gate, and `_pending_question`, awaited by `_user_input_callback` (:2036-2050) for the `ask_user_question` / `exit_plan_mode` tools. Those are scenarios 2.19/2.26 and 2.17/2.18 respectively — exactly the substitution this row forbids. There is no third.

`partial`, not `no`: the dialog class the row names does exist on vibe (trigger 2), so recording `no` would be false. `partial` records that it exists in a position where the row's arc is structurally unreachable.

## Daemon cannot observe it (daemon_capability: incapable)

Two independent reasons, either sufficient:

1. **There is usually no session at all.** vibe's Source is `FilesUnderRoot` over `~/.vibe/logs/session/<id>/messages.jsonl`, and that directory is created lazily inside `_save_interaction_sync` (core/session/session_logger.py:~255, `session_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)`) — i.e. on the first save, which cannot happen before the AgentLoop exists. During the trust dialog the only thing the daemon can see is the transient `proc-<PID>` presession row the CommandPattern scanner mints from the running `vibe` process, born `ready`. The row's FIRST assertion (`working`) is unproducible, not just its `waiting` leg.
2. **Even with a pre-existing session, nothing is written and no hook fires.** The one case worth naming, because a future assessor will try it: `vibe --continue` (or `--resume`) in an untrusted cwd, where the session directory already exists from a prior run so the daemon already holds a real session row. The trust dialog still blocks in `run_cli` before `load_session`; `messages.jsonl` is untouched; and the only hook irrlicht installs is `post_agent_turn` (core/adapters/inbound/agents/vibe/hooks.go), which fires at turn end. The session sits at `ready` for the whole dialog — coincidentally the right terminal state, which is precisely why a weakened spec asserting only "final state ready" would go green having observed nothing.

Not a `bug`: no spec-required observable is mis-handled. The dialog is outside the read path in both time and place.

## Driver is ready (driver_capability: ready)

`replaydata/agents/mistral-vibe/driver-interactive.sh:218` declares `DRIVE_ELICITS="send slash sleep wait_turn exit_clean restart sigkill resume keys start_session session interrupt"`. Answering a launch-time modal needs `keys` (present) after a `restart`/launch (present). The blocker is the daemon pillar, not a missing primitive — this cell must not be filed as a driver gap.

## Route

incapable daemon -> **frozen**. No recording is authored. Unfreezing requires an upstream change on the agent side first: vibe would have to raise a tool-less blocking dialog from INSIDE a live session (the way hermes' `_confirm_destructive_slash` does), and then irrlicht would need a channel that reports it — vibe's hook vocabulary is only `post_agent_turn` / `before_tool` / `after_tool` (core/hooks/models.py `HookType`), all three tool- or turn-scoped, so a new upstream hook type would be needed too.
caveats: LOAD-BEARING ENVIRONMENT PRECONDITION, and the vacuous-pass answer for this row: the trust dialog is SELF-SUPPRESSING. maybe_build_workspace_trust_prompt (core/trusted_folders.py:118-135) returns None when cwd resolves to $HOME, when trusted_folders_manager.is_trusted(cwd) is True, when cwd is explicitly untrusted, or when the directory contains no trustable files (no AGENTS.md and no project config). Answering it once persists the decision to ~/.vibe/trusted_folders.json (add_trusted / add_untrusted, :183-189), and --trust / --worktree / --add-dir all call trust_for_session up front (cli/entrypoint.py:329, :342). So on any host where the recording cwd was ever trusted, the dialog never opens, the session never leaves ready, and a spec asserting only the terminal ready would pass having tested nothing. Any future recording must re-probe ~/.vibe/trusted_folders.json for the recording cwd and assert the dialog actually appeared.

The second vacuous-pass condition is the substitution the scenario itself forbids: vibe's tool-permission dialog (_approval_callback, app.py:2008) and its ask_user_question dialog (_user_input_callback, :2036) look identical from the daemon's side. A recipe that reached either would satisfy nothing this row claims — those are 2.19/2.26 and 2.17/2.18.

agent_supports=partial rather than no is a deliberate call: the scenario instructs 'if the agent cannot raise any dialog of this kind, mark agent_supports: no', and vibe CAN raise one (the workspace trust prompt, the scenario's own trigger 2). What it cannot do is raise one from inside a live session. A future assessor who reads only the route should not conclude the dialog class is absent.

Every claim here is a source-read of the installed 2.19.1 package plus the adapter source; no vibe process was launched and no recording was run (this verb runs neither). The two absence claims (sandbox, MCP elicitation) rest on case-insensitive package-wide scans returning zero hits, which is the evidence a negative can carry — not a live probe. Confidence 0.8 reflects that.

CORRECTION carried from the 2-26 sibling, because the committed 2-19 cell states the opposite and is read first: vibe DOES have an HTTP hook channel (post_agent_turn, #1718) and DOES declare agent.Control. Neither helps this row — post_agent_turn fires at turn end — but the reason recorded here is the narrow one, not the stale 'no hook channel' one.

The mid-session inventory is bounded, not sampled: app.py holds exactly two asyncio.Future handles (self._pending_approval at :513, self._pending_question at :514) and both are tool-bound. If a future vibe release adds a third, this cell's agent pillar changes.

sources.note: THE ORDERING THAT DECIDES THIS CELL. _maybe_run_startup_update_prompt (:457) and resolve_trusted_folder() (:458-460) both run BEFORE load_session (:481) and before _run_interactive_mode (:485). No AgentLoop, no SessionLogger and no session directory exist while either dialog is on screen.

The trust dialog is raised from the entrypoint's resolve_trusted_folder callback. The only other blocking input() prompts in the package (worktree removal :223, branch deletion :241) run after run_cli returns, at teardown.

maybe_build_workspace_trust_prompt's suppression conditions ($HOME, already trusted, explicitly untrusted, no trustable files) and apply_workspace_trust_decision's persistence to TRUSTED_FOLDERS_FILE — the load-bearing precondition in the caveats.

The dialog itself: a Textual CenterMiddle widget with TRUST_REPO/TRUST_CWD/TRUST_SESSION/DECLINE options and a Decided message. This is the one tool-less blocking dialog vibe genuinely has — trigger 2 of the scenario's four.

The complete mid-session blocking inventory: exactly two futures, _pending_approval (tool permission gate, _approval_callback) and _pending_question (ask_user_question / exit_plan_mode, _user_input_callback). Both belong to a tool call, so both are the substitution this row forbids. No third exists.

sources.ref: mistral-vibe 2.19.1: package-wide scans for 'sandbox' and 'elicit' (case-insensitive, excluding __pycache__)
sources.note: Both return ZERO hits. Triggers 1 (sandbox/network confirmation) and 3 (server-driven MCP elicitation) are absent from vibe 2.19.1. Cited so a future audit does not re-litigate the negative.

The MCP-OAuth and connector-auth modals are raised from MCPApp.ConnectorAuthRequested / MCPOAuthRequested — the user's own /mcp slash command from the idle input app, never by the agent mid-turn. Same for the model/theme/thinking/config/proxy pickers (app.py:2654-2676).
plan_offer is CTA TEXT appended to a message body, not a blocking dialog — ruling out the 'auto-mode or settings review' trigger on the surface where it would most plausibly live.
The session directory is created lazily inside the save, so during a launch-time dialog no ~/.vibe/logs/session/<id>/ exists for the daemon's FilesUnderRoot Source to see.

vibe's ENTIRE hook vocabulary is post_agent_turn / before_tool / after_tool — all three tool- or turn-scoped. There is no event any agent-side dialog outside a tool call could ever fire, which is why unfreezing needs an upstream change, not just an adapter change.
irrlicht installs exactly one of those three: post_agent_turn -> HandleStopHook, which fires at turn end. Nothing reports a dialog opening.

Source = FilesUnderRoot over ~/.vibe/logs/session with a CommandPattern process matcher — the matcher is why a proc-<PID> presession row (born ready) is the only thing visible during a launch-time dialog.
DRIVE_ELICITS carries keys, restart, wait_turn and sleep — everything a launch-time modal recipe would need. driver=ready; the blocker is the daemon pillar.

Sibling precedent for the same row, and the contrast that sharpens this verdict: hermes raises its tool-less modals from INSIDE a live session (/clear, /reload-mcp, expensive /model switch) and still lands incapable on transport. vibe's are strictly launch-time, so it fails one pillar earlier.

recipe.note: Route is frozen on daemon=incapable — no recipe authored, and none could be written that satisfies the row today: vibe's only tool-less blocking dialogs (workspace trust, startup update prompt, teardown worktree y/N) all fire outside the AgentLoop, so no `send` can elicit one and no live session exists to move working -> waiting. Do NOT substitute vibe's tool-permission dialog or its ask_user_question dialog to make this cell recordable — the scenario forbids exactly that, and those belong to 2.19/2.26 and 2.17/2.18. Re-assess only if a future vibe release raises a tool-less blocking dialog from inside a live session AND exposes an event for it (its hook vocabulary today is only post_agent_turn / before_tool / after_tool). If that happens, any recipe must first re-probe ~/.vibe/trusted_folders.json for the recording cwd — a previously-trusted cwd suppresses the trust dialog entirely and would make the cell pass while observing nothing.
